column2: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time and is a vector quantity with both magnitude and direction.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by a resultant external force.
The resultant force on an object is equal to the rate of change of its momentum (F = ma for constant mass).
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity (p = mv).
In a closed system, total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after.
Work done is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force (W = Fs).
Kinetic energy is the energy an object has due to its motion (Ek = 1/2 mv^2).
Energy stored due to an object's position in a gravitational field (Ep = mgh).
Power is the rate of doing work or energy transfer (P = W/t).
The extension of a spring is proportional to the force applied, provided the limit of proportionality is not exceeded.
Stress is force per unit area (σ = F/A).
Strain is the ratio of extension to original length.
Density is mass per unit volume (ρ = m/V).
Pressure is force per unit area (P = F/A).
For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume.
For a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature.
Energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1°C or 1K.
Energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance without temperature change.
A wave is a transfer of energy through oscillations without net movement of matter.
The distance between two consecutive points in phase on a wave.
The number of oscillations per second.
Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength (v = fλ).
The change in direction of a wave as it passes from one medium to another due to speed change.
The spreading of waves as they pass through a gap or around an obstacle.
The superposition of two waves to form a resultant wave.
The rate of flow of charge (I = Q/t).
Work done per unit charge (V = W/Q).
Current is proportional to potential difference provided temperature remains constant (V = IR).
Resistance is the ratio of potential difference to current (R = V/I).
Power is the rate of energy transfer in a circuit (P = IV).
Force per unit charge (E = F/Q).
Force per unit mass (g = F/m).
Force per unit current per unit length on a conductor at right angles to a magnetic field.
